body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「客戶話 assistant『成日 hallucinate』。頭 48 小時你會做乜？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會換更強的 model。」

『Hallucinate』往往是多種 failure 的總稱：答了不存在的事、引用不支持、拿了過期 source、漏了權限、把不確定 case 講得太肯定，或者其實是 user 以為它可以做一個從未承諾的 action。直接換 model 不會令你知道是哪種錯、誰受影響、以及下一次怎樣辨認它。頭兩日的任務是把抱怨變成可重現、可處置的事實。

## 先穩住後果，再收集樣本

若系統會發送、寫入、建議高風險決定，先將它收窄成 draft-only、require-confirmation 或暫停相應 route；不要為了 debug 而繼續擴大影響。跟客戶確認一小組已去識別化或 synthetic examples、發生時間、user role、預期資訊來源、實際 output 和造成的阻塞。清楚說明目前不知道甚麼，也不要拿客戶資料去一個未批准的外部工具重播。

## 把一句抱怨變成 failure ledger

為每個 case 寫 outcome class：missing evidence、wrong source、stale source、permission breach、unsupported inference、format／tool failure、或 expectation mismatch。留 request receipt：版本、input 摘要、role、retrieved source IDs、tool calls、output、latency 和 human correction。每類先揀一個 representative case；若只有模糊截圖，先建立收集和 redaction route，而不是把它硬塞進一個 model eval。

## 在 48 小時內選一個可逆實驗

對最嚴重又可重現的一類，列 baseline、candidate 和 acceptance test。例如 citation 不支持時，candidate 可以是先驗證 source IDs 再顯示草稿；permission breach 則要修 filter／service control，非調 prompt。用固定 cases 比較，保留 human reviewer 和 stop rule。若 evidence 還不夠，就維持收窄 route，並說明下一批要收集甚麼；這也是一個正確的 delivery decision。

## 面試時給對方一條時間線

『第一日我會把後果性 route 收窄，和對方對齊可安全使用的案例與失敗定義；第二日把 case 連同 trace 放入 failure ledger，挑一類做 baseline/candidate 比較，未達 acceptance 就不擴大。』這不是避開技術，而是先令 retrieval、prompt、model、permission 或 workflow fix 有正確的靶。

## 你在示範的，不止 debugging

- **工程：** redacted case format、failure taxonomy、trace receipt、fixed regression cases、acceptance test 和 candidate diff。
- **交付：** 哪個 route 已收窄、誰可 review、向客戶怎樣交代 unknown、何時 re-enable 或延長暫停。
- **邊界：** 一個不重現的模糊抱怨不會被假裝成 model metric；你先建立可安全收集 evidence 的方法。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “A customer says the assistant hallucinates all the time. What would you do in the first 48 hours?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would switch to a stronger model.”

‘Hallucination’ is often a bundle of failures: an invented fact, unsupported citation, stale source, permission miss, uncertain case stated too confidently, or an expectation that the system can take an action it never promised. Replacing the model does not tell you which error occurred, who was affected, or how to recognise it next time. The first two days turn a complaint into reproducible, actionable facts.

## Stabilise consequences before gathering samples

If the system sends, writes or recommends a high-risk decision, narrow it to draft-only, require-confirmation, or pause the relevant route. Do not expand impact while debugging. Agree with the customer on a small set of de-identified or synthetic examples, the time, user role, expected information source, actual output and blocked decision. State what is not yet known; do not replay customer data through an unapproved external tool.

## Turn one complaint into a failure ledger

For each case, write an outcome class: missing evidence, wrong source, stale source, permission breach, unsupported inference, format/tool failure or expectation mismatch. Keep a request receipt: version, input summary, role, retrieved source IDs, tool calls, output, latency and human correction. Choose one representative case per class. If you only have a vague screenshot, build a collection and redaction route first rather than force it into a model evaluation.

## Choose one reversible experiment within 48 hours

For the most severe reproducible class, name a baseline, candidate and acceptance test. For an unsupported citation, a candidate might verify source IDs before showing a draft. A permission breach calls for a filter/service control, not a prompt tweak. Compare fixed cases, retain a human reviewer and stop rule. If evidence remains insufficient, keep the narrowed route and state what the next sample must capture; that is also a correct delivery decision.

## Give the interviewer a time line

‘On day one I narrow consequential routes and align on safely usable cases and a failure definition. On day two I add cases and traces to a failure ledger, choose one class for a baseline/candidate comparison, and do not expand until it meets acceptance.’ That is not avoiding technical work; it gives retrieval, prompt, model, permission or workflow work the correct target.

## What you are demonstrating beyond debugging

- **Engineering:** a redacted-case format, failure taxonomy, trace receipt, fixed regression cases, acceptance test and candidate diff.
- **Delivery:** which route is narrowed, who can review, how unknowns are explained to the customer, and when to re-enable or extend the pause.
- **Boundary:** a vague complaint that cannot be reproduced is not pretended to be a model metric; you first create a safe way to collect evidence.

## Further reading

[Why did a stable prompt fail when the context changed?](/en/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test), [The offline score improved. Why did the human workflow not?](/en/interview-lab/offline-score-and-human-workflow), and [After changing the model, how do you choose release or rollback?](/en/interview-lab/release-or-rollback-with-evidence).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Customers, cases, traces and delivery steps are fictional synthetic teaching material; they are not a customer incident, service commitment or production-support guidance.
